articles.title: Apuestas y pronósticos Croacia vs España
articles.standfirst: Codere te ofrece el pronóstico del partido que enfrenta a Croacia y España en el Stadion Poljud correspondiente a la jornada 4 del Grupo 3 de la Liga A de la Nations League
articles.summary: Codere te ofrece el pronóstico del partido que enfrenta a Croacia y España en el Stadion Poljud correspondiente a la jornada 4 del Grupo 3 de la Liga A de la Nations League
articles.body: Croacia afronta esta cuarta jornada de la Nations League después de sufrir la mayor goleada de su historia frente a Inglaterra. El conjunto balcánico llega, por tanto, obligado a reaccionar después de un resultado especialmente doloroso y con la necesidad de recuperar sensaciones. Enfrente tendrá a una España que continúa liderando el grupo y con una racha de invencibilidad que no parece tener fin. Favorito para el partido entre Croacia y España La selección española viene de lograr una victoria sufrida frente a la República Checa. Un resultado que le permite mantenerse asentada en lo más alto de la clasificación. Además, el combinado de Luis de la Fuente cuenta con el precedente del partido de ida, en el que goleó a Croacia. Las casas de apuestas conceden un claro favoritismo a España: Codere ofrece una cuota de 9.00 por la victoria croata, 5.50 por el empate y 1.28 por el triunfo español. Ambos equipos marcan El mercado de ambos equipos marcan aparece como una opción interesante en las apuestas deportivas. Especialmente, teniendo en cuenta la dinámica de ambas selecciones. Croacia ha cumplido este pronóstico en dos de sus tres partidos de esta Nations League, mientras que España lo ha hecho en todos sus encuentros. Además, ambos equipos consiguieron ver portería en el enfrentamiento de ida, lo que refuerza la posibilidad de volver a encontrar goles en las dos áreas. Codere ofrece una cuota de 1.80 por el 'sí' y de 1.90 por el 'no'. Número total de goles (Over/Under) La línea de goles presenta una tendencia todavía más clara. En todos los partidos disputados por Croacia en esta Nations League se han superado los 2.5 goles totales. Exactamente, el mismo registro que presenta España. Esta circunstancia también se produjo en el encuentro de ida, en el que el conjunto español se impuso con un marcador amplio. Todo ello apunta hacia un nuevo duelo con posibilidades de superar la línea de goles. Codere paga a 1.45 que se marquen más de 2.5 goles y a 2.60 que se registren menos de 2.5 tantos. Número total de córners (Over/Under) El mercado de córners ofrece, en cambio, una tendencia bastante más contenida. En ninguno de los partidos disputados por Croacia en esta Nations League se han superado los 9.5 lanzamientos de esquina, un registro que también se repite en todos los encuentros de España. Además, el partido de ida entre ambos combinados terminó con un total de ocho córners, por debajo de la línea planteada para este encuentro. Codere ofrece una cuota de 1.88 por que se superen los 9.5 córners y de 1.75 por que haya menos.

articles.title: Why Pittsburgh Penguins star Evgeni Malkin broke tradition following Alex Ovechkin’s Washington Capitals NHL retirement announcement
articles.summary: Evgeni Malkin speaks out following Alex Ovechkin's retirement announcement, marking a significant moment in their rivalry and the NHL's history. Discover the implications for both players and the Pittsburgh Penguins as the Capitals star sets to end his legendary career.
articles.body: The announcement immediately became one of the biggest NHL updates of the week. Alex Ovechkin confirmed that the 2026-27 season will be his final campaign with the Washington Capitals, bringing his 22-year NHL career toward its conclusion. The news also carried significance for the Pittsburgh Penguins, who have shared one of the league’s most recognizable rivalries with Washington throughout the careers of Ovechkin and Evgeni Malkin.For Evgeni Malkin, the announcement prompted an unusual decision. The Pittsburgh Penguins star broke his established routine of not speaking with reporters after morning skates, choosing instead to discuss Ovechkin and what his retirement means for their generation of NHL players.Evgeni Malkin spoke about Alex Ovechkin’s retirementEvgeni Malkin said Alex Ovechkin’s retirement will be difficult to see because of what the Washington Capitals captain has accomplished for his team and the NHL. Malkin also wished his longtime rival and friend good health during his final season.Malkin’s decision reflected the significance of Ovechkin’s announcement. For roughly two decades, the Pittsburgh Penguins center has generally avoided speaking to reporters following morning skates. Monday’s retirement news was important enough for him to change that routine.The two players have been connected since the 2004 NHL Draft. Ovechkin was selected No. 1 overall by the Washington Capitals, while Malkin went second to the Pittsburgh Penguins. Their careers subsequently developed alongside one another, creating years of memorable regular-season and playoff matchups.Malkin acknowledged that the relationship between the two Russian stars was not always perfect. However, he said past disagreements are behind them and emphasized that they have become good friends who support each other and their families.That evolution adds another dimension to the Penguins-Capitals rivalry. What began with two highly touted Russian prospects being selected first and second in the same draft eventually became a relationship marked by competition, mutual respect and friendship.What does Ovechkin’s final season mean for Pittsburgh?The Washington Capitals and Pittsburgh Penguins are scheduled to meet four times during the 2026-27 regular season. Their first meeting comes Wednesday in Washington, making the matchup particularly significant given Ovechkin’s retirement announcement.Malkin said games against Ovechkin have always felt special and acknowledged that the eventual retirement will be a sad moment. The remaining matchups now carry added importance because they represent some of the final opportunities for two players who entered the NHL in the same era to face one another.Malkin also offered an intriguing reflection about his own future. At 40, he acknowledged that this could potentially be his final NHL season as well, although he emphasized that he still loves playing hockey. That uncertainty gives the Penguins-Capitals meetings another storyline to follow throughout the season.The immediate focus, however, remains on Ovechkin. The NHL’s all-time leading goal scorer is entering his final campaign, while Malkin and the Penguins prepare for a season in which every meeting with the Washington Capitals could become part of hockey history.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Victor Wembanyama: NBA star trains with rugby club
articles.summary: NBA superstar Victor Wembanyama says he was inspired by the unity and camaraderie of rugby after spending time with French second tier side Provence.
articles.body:
NBA superstar Victor Wembanyama says he was inspired by the unity and camaraderie of rugby after spending part of his summer off-season training with French second tier side Provence.

The 22-year-old Frenchman, who is 7ft 4in and 16st 11lbs, is known for his off-beat search for ways to improve his game. He spent a fortnight focusing on physical and mental strength with Shaolin monks in China in 2025. , external

Footage shows Wembanyama , external hitting tackle pads, going through passing drills, taking part in a line-out and looming over the rest of the Provence team in a huddle before a pre-season friendly in August.

He was also filmed sharing a dressing-room embrace with former England international Teimana Harrison, who won five England caps in 2016 and now plays for Provence.

"It was a great experience, seeing the team spirit they have over there," said Wembanyama, , external who was joined on the trip by San Antonio Spurs' team-mate Harrison Barnes.

"It was very inspiring to see the relationship between team-mates, coaches and fans. The training was really hard, really good for stability, movement patterns and developing strength, but I am more grateful for the experience of how I was welcomed there.

"I have never been welcomed anywhere like this. I wasn't part of the team but they treated me like I was. I want to do it again."

Wembanyama combined his work with Provence with hosting his Hoop Gambit event, in which participants play games of chess and basketball, in his hometown of Le Chesnay.

Wembanyama's Spurs fell just short of the NBA Championship earlier this year, going down 4-1 to the New York Knicks in June.

Provence, who previously have been represented by Wales internationals George North and Tomas Francis, have begun their season and search for promotion to the Top 14 well, winning their first five league games.

articles.title: Así quedó la grama de El Campín tras los conciertos de BTS en Bogotá: la decisión que afecta a Santa Fe
articles.standfirst: Preocupación en Bogotá: filtran imágenes de cómo quedó el césped de El Campín tras el paso de BTS
articles.summary: Preocupación en Bogotá: filtran imágenes de cómo quedó el césped de El Campín tras el paso de BTS
articles.body: Los cuatro conciertos consecutivos de la agrupación surcoreana BTS en Bogotá marcaron un hito sin precedentes para la industria del entretenimiento en Colombia, reuniendo a más de 160.000 espectadores en el estadio Nemesio Camacho El Campín. Sin embargo, tras el retiro de las estructuras del escenario y de la teleras de protección, la imagen de la gramilla ha generado inquietud entre los aficionados al fútbol capitalino. El uso intensivo durante cuatro jornadas consecutivas, sumado a las pesadas infraestructuras de montaje y al constante tráfico de personas en el área de cancha, dejó evidentes secuelas en el césped: Ante el deterioro visual del terreno de juego, Sencia —la APP encargada de la administración y renovación del escenario deportivo— activó de inmediato un plan de contingencia agrónomico para recuperar la gramilla en un plazo máximo de 10 días. El plan de restauración comprende las siguientes fases: La principal urgencia recae en la reprogramación de los compromisos de Independiente Santa Fe y Millonarios. Aunque las directivas de Sencia aseguran que la cancha estará apta para el desarrollo del FPC dentro del lapso fijado, la evolución climática de Bogotá durante los próximos días será crucial para determinar si los equipos capitalinos podrán disputar sus compromisos en las fechas programadas o si se requerirán ajustes de última hora en el calendario. Por lo pronto se estima que mientras dure la recuperación de la grama de el Campín, Santa Fe traslade su compromiso contra Fortaleza, que tendrá lugar el próximo 11 de octubre, al estadio Municipal de Techo.

articles.title: Saints vs. Falcons Game MVP
articles.summary: The fans showed up for the Saints, unfortunately the game didn't go as expected.
articles.body:
In all honesty, after getting your teeth kicked in the way the Saints just did in primetime, there really isn't a player of the game. It is worth noting that Chris Olave played great again, but that's not worth much when the team gets embarrassed the way it just did.

The true MVPs of this game, however, were the fans.

Shoutout to the entire city of New Orleans, which was on 10 from the moment the sun came up. New Orleans was ready and excited for what this game represented: the 20-year celebration of the reopening of the Superdome after Hurricane Katrina.

The atmosphere inside the Dome at kickoff was electric. I spoke with former Saints wide receiver Lance Moore after the game, and he said the Dome felt like the Dome again. And that is exactly what it should be.

The fans were ready to roll. The excitement was there, and every single one of you, whether you were at home, at work, or at the stadium, just wanted that moment to shout, "Who Dat!"

The Saints did a great job of having Steve Gleason lead the Who Dat chant at the start of the game, with his son by his side raising his hand. The emotions were nearly overwhelming as a fan, seeing all of the pageantry that went into this game. The former players from 20 years ago were present on the sideline for kickoff. It was beautiful to see.

All of that went away because, for the next three hours, the play on the field did not match the expectations and hope that Saints fans had going into the night.

Who Dat Nation, you all are this week's Canal Street Chronicles MVP.

articles.title: Lewis Hamilton can overtake George Russell for second in F1 title race as Mercedes penalty opens the door in Singapore
articles.summary: Lewis Hamilton has a real chance to take second place in the Formula 1 drivers' championship from George Russell this weekend. Mercedes has confirmed that Ru...
articles.body:
Lewis Hamilton has a real chance to take second place in the Formula 1 drivers' championship from George Russell this weekend. Mercedes has confirmed that Russell will start Sunday's Singapore Grand Prix from the back of the grid, and the Ferrari driver trails him by just 22 points.

Mercedes confirmed that Russell needs a new power unit after his retirement in Malaysia, as GPBlog reported in Russell hit hard by PU change: heavy grid penalty confirmed for Singapore . The team has confirmed that Russell will take the new unit in Singapore and start from the back.

After Sepang, Kimi Antonelli leads on 320 points. Russell has 236 and Hamilton 214. Russell scored nothing after his late engine failure, while Hamilton finished third after battling back from the pack, with GPblog's analysis showing how Hamilton overruled Ferrari's pit wall at Sepang and how that recovery played out to give him some momentum heading to Singapore.

Singapore is the last Sprint weekend of 2026, so there are more points on offer than usual. The Sprint pays eight points to the winner down to one for eighth place, and a Grand Prix win is worth 25. That means one driver can score at most 33 points across the weekend. GPblog used the same figure to show how Antonelli can't be crowned in Singapore but also explained how it keeps Hamilton in the hunt for second place.

To move up to second outright, Hamilton has to score 23 points more than Russell. Beating him by 22 would only put them level. Even a perfect double would take Hamilton to 247 points, so if Russell scores 11 points or more, the Mercedes driver keeps second place for at least another round.

Here's how the points would shake out in the drivers' championship in Singapore

Hamilton wins both the Sprint and the Grand Prix (33 points): Russell must score 10 points or fewer.

Hamilton wins the Grand Prix and finishes third in the Sprint (31 points): Russell must score 8 points or fewer.

Hamilton finishes second in both races (25 points): Russell must score 2 points or fewer.

Hamilton finishes third in both races (21 points): not enough, because a pointless Russell would still lead him by one point.

Lewis Hamilton givin his team the okay in Singapore. Photo: RacePictures.

The Sprint is Russell's best chance to hold on

Russell gets one opportunity to protect his position before the penalty applies as the penalty will be served in Sunday's Grand Prix, not the Sprint, so on Saturday he will start from wherever he qualifies.

That could be key because Russell has been the strongest Sprint driver this season. He has won three of the five Sprints so far, in China, Canada and the Netherlands. If he wins on Saturday, Hamilton would need second place in the Sprint and victory on Sunday, and Russell would have to finish outside the points in the Grand Prix.

Sunday is a different story as overtaking at Marina Bay is notoriously difficult, which makes starting from the back a big handicap. Russell knows the circuit well, though: he won the 2025 Singapore Grand Prix from pole position, but this season it could be too great a task.

articles.title: Fantasy Football Week 5 Tight End Waiver Wire Targets: Prioritize T.J. Hockenson
articles.summary: T.J. Hockenson and these other two tight ends are worth targeting on the fantasy football waiver wire entering Week 5.
articles.body:
Some fantasy football managers are lucky enough to have Brock Bowers locked into their tight end spot, essentially giving them another wide receiver in the lineup. Aside from Bowers, Trey McBride remains a consistent source of fantasy production, and George Kittle is excelling in an efficient offense.

If you don't roster any of the premier TEs in fantasy football, which TEs should you target on the waiver wire in Week 5?

All stats used in this article are from PFF or Sumer Sports unless stated otherwise. Fantasy rankings and fantasy point totals are courtesy of FantasyPros .

T.J. Hockenson turned back the clock a bit in Week 4, producing a TE1 finish with 24.9 fantasy points on 13 receptions and 119 receiving yards. The Kyler Murray-led aerial attack for the Minnesota Vikings is still in the adjustment phase, and Murray is building a decent rapport with Hockenson.

While Justin Jefferson will undoubtedly be the No. 1 target for Murray when he returns from injury, Hockenson can emerge as the No. 2 option ahead of Jordan Addison. Next up for Hockenson and the Vikings are the New Orleans Saints, who are 28th in dropback EPA (0.22) and 30th in dropback success rate (52.4%) allowed this season.

Brenton Strange logged a season-best 16.5 fantasy points in Week 4, tying Tucker Kraft as the TE5. While Strange is still just the TE21 in fantasy points per game (9.2) entering Week 5, he's part of an ultra-efficient passing attack with Trevor Lawrence dealing for the Jacksonville Jaguars.

Of the 25 TEs with 15-plus targets this season, Strange has the sixth-most yards per reception (11.9) and seventh-most yards per route run (1.86).

Both Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins picked up injuries in Week 4 for the Cincinnati Bengals, and it remains to be seen what their statuses will be in Week 5 against the Miami Dolphins. If Chase and/or Higgins are sidelined on Sunday, Mike Gesicki stands out as a solid waiver-wire option.

Aside from this week's matchup being a revenge game for Gesicki, he's the TE13 in fantasy points per game (11.1) with 12-plus fantasy points in three of his first four starts in 2026.

articles.body:
St. Thomas Aquinas is still the No. 1 ranked football team in Florida, but IMG is closing the gap.

The Raiders, which have been the top-ranked team in the state since the preseason, received nine first-place votes to hold onto the No. 1 spot in the USA TODAY Florida Super 25 heading into Week 8.

articles.title: The 49ers will be without Kyle Juszczyk vs. Seahawks in Week 5
articles.summary: The San Francisco 49ers will be without FB Kyle Juszczyk versus the Seattle Seahawks in Week 5.
articles.body:
The Seattle Seahawks play a critical divisional game in Week 5 . They'll host their NFC West rival San Francisco 49ers at Lumen Field. The 3-1 Seahawks currently trail the perfect 4-0 49ers in the division.

Fortunately for the Seahawks, Kyle Shanahan's offense will be without a critical playmaker. Fullback Kyle Juszczyk will miss the Week 5 game versus Seattle. An MRI recently revealed that Juszczyk has a knee sprain and bone bruise that will sideline him for multiple weeks, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter.

The 49ers offense is currently averaging 137.3 rushing yards per game. That ranks sixth-best in the entire NFL. Juszczyk is often a big reason why Coach Shanahan fields such an effective ground attack. Juszczyk consistently generates rushing lanes for Christian McCaffrey.

The Seahawks are dealing with injuries of their own. Head coach Mike Macdonald recently provided health updates on Leonard Williams and Zach Charbonnet. Getting Williams back for the 49ers game is critical to slowing down McCaffrey and the 49ers' rushing offense.

The NFC West is so competitive. The division title may be decided by the games between the Seahawks, 49ers, and Los Angeles Rams. The Seahawks won't exactly be sad to hear the 49ers won't have Juszczyk on Sunday.

articles.title: 3 Reasons Why the Chicago Bears Won vs. the New York Jets
articles.summary: Chicago grinded out another home win this week without their start QB. @BryanOrenchuk shares his 3 reasons the Bears earned the W.
articles.body:
Welcome back to the fourth installment of my new series for the 2026 season, where I recap what I believe were the three reasons the Chicago Bears won or lost the previous game.

In week 4, the Bears hosted the feisty New York Jets and controlled the game from start to finish, dominating the time of possession and coming away with a gritty win once again without Caleb Williams as he recovers from his hamstring injury. Here are my three reasons why they won.

Though the 2nd year player out of Rutgers has had one game where he had more rushing yards than the 149 he racked up on the ground against the Jets, and five games where he did so with more yards per carry than the 4.9 he had, he has never scored more than once like he did and never had 30 carries before either. Considering he was clearly the best player on the field for both teams, I will henceforth be referring to this performance as the "Monangai Game" until further notice.

What impressed me most about the New Jersey native was the nature by which his success came. He was getting met at or behind the line of scrimmage early in this one and ended the first half with only 49 yards rushing. But he seemed to get stronger as the game wore on, consistently bouncing off would-be tacklers or peeling away from them for extra yardage before sporadic bursts through the line for chunk gains. You could tell he was wearing on the defense and clearly Ben Johnson could tell as well considering he saw 30 carries to D'Andre Swift's 15. On a day where the Bears struggled to put the ball in the endzone and score TDs, Monangai seemed like the difference in this one and the main reason Chicago came away with a W. Shout out to the offensive line for continuing to pound away at the formidable Jets defensive line and the wide receivers and tight ends for committing to the gameplan as well. When you have a back like Monangai, you never know when he will break away and use your block for more yardage.

Speaking of best games, this was easily Rome's best game of the season as well. What stood out to me regarding Odunze's performance, aside from marveling at how a WR his size (6'3", 215lb) moves in and out of his breaks, was how seamlessly he caught the ball this week and the clutch nature of his catches. All game, it seemed like Rome was coming up big on 3rd down and was a large reason why we were able to move the ball down the field, especially in the first half before Monangai took over. Rome's 94 receiving yards paced both teams in this one, and he did so on just 7 targets with 6 catches for 15.7 yards per catch and a season-best 85.7 catch percentage. Rome played with confidence and power as both a pass-catcher and run-blocker, and his presence was felt throughout this win.

On a day when the offense struggled to find the endzone, especially in the red zone, it sure was nice to have such an automatic kicker on your side. Especially in the Windy City, with gusts coming off the lake as they do. Though none of his kicks were longer than 30 yards, Santos helped keep this game out of reach for a Jets comeback. Without Santos, I am not sure Ben elects to kick the FG which made it a three score game in the 4th quarter, which could have changed the entire outcome in this one. Ben trusts him, and his teammates do too, and it showed up this week.

What about you? Who or what caught your attention against the Jets?

articles.title: Armagh's Mackin shortlisted for Players' POTY award
articles.summary: Armagh's Aimee Mackin, Olivia Divilly from Galway and Kerry captain Siofra O'Shea are nominated for the LGFA Senior Players' Player of the Year Award.
articles.body:
Armagh's Aimee Mackin has been nominated for the 2026 TG4 Senior Players' Player of the Year Award alongside Galway's Olivia Divilly and Kerry captain Siofra O'Shea.

Mackin registered 5-12 in four games during the All-Ireland series to help Armagh progress to the semi-finals.

All-Ireland winner Divilly scored three points in the final against Kerry to help the Tribeswomen win the Brendan Martin Cup for the first time since 2004.

Kerry's O'Shea is also shortlisted and was top scorer this season with the winner announced in Dublin on Saturday, 14 November.

All three players have also been nominated for All-Stars with a total of six players from Armagh nominated, while Galway have 14 nominees in the 45-player long list.

In the intermediate category, All-Ireland Intermediate Final player of the match, Saoirse Wynne, Fermanagh's Eimear Smyth and Westmeath's Anna Jones have been shortlisted for player of the year.

In the junior grade, Carlow duo Roisin Bailey and Sara Doyle and Antrim's All-Ireland final match-winner Maria O'Neill are nominated.

The nominees in all three categories were selected by fellow inter-county players, who could not vote for their own team-mates.

Intermediate Players' Player of the Year Award Nominees: Eimear Smyth (Fermanagh), Saoirse Wynne (Roscommon), Anna Jones (Westmeath)

Junior Players' Player of the Year Award Nominees: Maria O'Neill (Antrim), Roisin Bailey (Carlow), Sara Doyle (Carlow)

articles.title: Fred Claire, Dodgers GM whose Kirk Gibson signing created iconic moment, dies
articles.summary: Fred Claire, who guided the Dodgers through a pivotal era and helped assemble the 1988 World Series winners, dies at the age of 91.
articles.body:
Fred Claire, the former Los Angeles Dodgers general manager whose signing of Kirk Gibson led to one of the most iconic moments in baseball history, died Monday, Oct. 5, the Dodgers announced. He was 91.

Claire took over the Dodgers franchise at a most tumultuous time - after longtime general manager and vice president Al Campanis was fired for racist remarks made on ABC's Nightline. His April 9, 1987 dismissal ended an era of front office stability while the Dodgers embarked on a fourth consecutive year missing the playoffs.

Claire, a former sportswriter and Dodgers PR man, was tabbed to run the front office. A pair of transactions in the year that followed shaped the Dodgers' eventual 1988 championship core: A three-way winter meetings trade with the Oakland Athletics and New York Mets that netted the Dodgers relievers Jesse Orosco and Jay Howell and shortstop Alfredo Griffin.

Those Dodgers won 94 games, stunned the Mets in the National League Championship Series and pulled an even bigger shocker in the 1988 World Series, beating the A's in five games despite a battered club that came to rely on ace Orel Hershiser and an itinerant band of ballplayers known as the "Stuntmen."

And they only had Gibson for one at-bat - but he made the most of it. Gibson's two-out, two-run, ninth-inning homer off peerless closer Dennis Eckersley delivered the Dodgers a Game 1 win and the 104-win A's never recovered.

Claire held his position for a decade, ushered out unceremoniously after Fox bought the club and dickered over the re-signing of Mike Piazza. Piazza's trade to the Florida Marlins was brokered above Claire's head. He was fired weeks later.

Claire remained a well-regarded baseball mind, and later in life documented his journey through cancer treatments , eventually penning an autobiography, "Extra Innings," that detailed his life in baseball and his battle against the disease.

He is survived by his wife Cheryl and children Jeff, Jennifer and Kim.

"The Dodgers are grieving the passing of Fred Claire, a longtime key fixture of our organization," said Stan Kasten, President and CEO of the Dodgers, in a statement released by the club. "Fred brought many victories and Dodger legends to our franchise, as well as a 1988 World Series title, and we are forever grateful for his leadership during such a memorable era. Our hearts go out to his wife Sheryl and his family."

articles.title: Excl: Arsenal in talks with Nicolas Jover over new deal
articles.summary: Arsenal have been in negotiations with Nicolas Jover over a contract extension during the international break, following Mikel Arteta’s agreement on a new de...
articles.body:
Arsenal have been in negotiations with Nicolas Jover over a contract extension during the international break, following Mikel Arteta's agreement on a new deal.

Daily Cannon understands that Andrea Berta has been leading negotiations with Arsenal set-piece coach Nicolas Jover over a new contract during the international break, with the club keen to extend the deals of Mikel Arteta's assistants.

Arsenal's staff and players remain very much aligned on the value of set-pieces, and the club are willing to recognise that with a good contract.

Previous reports at the start of the break had suggested that Arteta's backroom staff would sign four-year deals, in line with the manager's own reported new contract to 2030. But Daily Cannon's understanding is that talks were still ongoing during the break.

Jover has developed a special methodology for Arsenal's set-piece training and implementation, and the club clearly want to keep him around.

It's possible that Arsenal's desire to extend the contracts of all of Arteta's backroom staff is behind the delay in the announcement for the manager's own new deal.

Sami Mokbel had broken the news for the BBC on September 22nd that Arteta had agreed a new contract, bringing to an end negotiations that had been ongoing for a number of months.

Fabrizio Romano reported on Monday that Arteta is ready to put pen to paper, but that still doesn't seem to have happened at the time of writing.

With no official announcement and nothing formally signed, the only thing currently tying Arteta to Arsenal beyond the summer of 2027 is his verbal agreement with the club.

But given how well things have been going for all parties in 2026 so far, and with a substantial pay increase on the table, the expectation is that the formalities will be concluded soon.

articles.title: Juventus & Napoli to Address Their Midfields in January
articles.summary: Juventus and Napoli are making preparations ahead of January, and both teams aim to shore up their midfields because of some injury blows. The Bianconeri won...
articles.body:
Juventus and Napoli are making preparations ahead of January, and both teams aim to shore up their midfields because of some injury blows. The Bianconeri won't have Khephren Thuram and Manuel Locatelli for months, while Frank Anguissa and Scott McTominay have had some problems for the Partenopei .

According to La Gazzetta dello Sport , the Old Lady is particularly keen on Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg. Luciano Spalletti wants a veteran leader. Former free agents Leon Goretzka and Frank Kessié have latched onto other clubs.

Olympique Marseille are in a financial crunch, so the Dane isn't untouchable despite being the captain and a pillar. Their new CEO Giovanni Carnevali has done a lot of business with the French club, signing Ismael Koné, Ulisses Garcia, and Darryl Bakola during his time with Sassuolo.

Napoli are also in the hunt for a midfielder, but they plan to go younger than Juventus. They have shortlisted Monaco's Mamadou Coulibaly. His physicality would come in handy. He has registered 4 goals and 7 assists in 47 matches with his current team.

The possible fallback is Union Saint-Gilloise's Adem Zorgane, who will turn 27 in January. He's a staple with Algeria and can handle multiple roles. The Azzurri are also keeping tabs on Dodo, who might depart Fiorentina for cheap to avoid a Bosman exit.

They are both in trouble in the role, and the Azzurri appear headed for a significant overhaul at the end of the campaign. They'd better start bringing in quality reinforcements as soon as they can, and they are already one man short. Hojbjerg would be a fine addition, but the buzz linking him to Serie A has never amounted to much in the past.

articles.title: Lakers insider reveals real reason why Wizards' Anthony Davis gained weight after latest comment
articles.summary: Former Los Angeles Lakers NBA champion Anthony Davis revealed that he was having to gain weight to play center during his time with the organization. A Laker...
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Lakers are now in the Luka Doncic era, and the process of it started in early 2025. Doncic was playing with the Dallas Mavericks when the most shocking trade in NBA history went down.

The Lakers made a trade for Doncic that shipped out Anthony Davis.

"The Dallas Mavericks are trading Luka Doncic, Maxi Kleber and Markieff Morris to the Los Angeles Lakers for Anthony Davis, Max Christie and a 2029 first-round pick, sources tell ESPN. Three-team deal that includes Utah," ESPN's Shams Charania posted.

This ended Davis' long tenure in LA, one where he played center for most of his career. Davis revealed that he had to gain weight to play center, and it just didn't work out with his body.

"The strength training I was doing because I knew I was playing center, like I'm going against Joel Embiid and Jokic. And I never like I've always played like 250. And that year I had got to like 265 and it was like I didn't like it. It was actually probably like 268 and I didn't like it. I'm like, bro, I can't play like this. I feel heavy. So I tried to cut during the season but when when you trying to do that while you playing this it was tough. And then that's when I went and was like hey man I want another big and all this stuff and you know it just didn't happen whatever," Davis said.

However, Lakers insider Anthony F. Irwin reported that Davis gained weight because he stopped working hard.

"AD didn't gain weight because the Lakers asked him to play center. He gained the weight because he stopped working as hard on keeping the weight off. He then had to play center because he couldn't move his feet quite as well and forgot how to shoot," Irwin posted.

This situation now has another layer to it, as a Lakers insider has called Davis out for not taking care of himself when it matters the most. Davis' tenure with LA did come to a screaming halt.

It seems like behind the scenes, Davis was doing whatever it took to get the Lakers to stop playing him at center. The more this drags on, the messier the relationship between the two seems to get.

articles.title: College football prediction market picks, upset bets for Week 6
articles.summary: Two Saturday clashes between unbeaten teams headline this week's six prediction market selections, with three more games kicking off Friday night out West.
articles.body:
Week 6 college football prediction market picks back Alabama, FIU, Washington and Utah State as favorites, while Iowa State and Nebraska carry upset paths built on injuries, soft schedules and steady market support.

The biggest swing came in Tuscaloosa, where No. 2 Georgia opened as a 3-point favorite before No. 6 Alabama flipped the line after a 56-23 win at Mississippi State. Both teams enter Saturday night's matchup at 5-0.

FIU and Utah State have drawn the steadiest support among this week's favorites, as both spreads have climbed 2.5 points since opening. Meanwhile, Iowa State and Nebraska have each gained at least 2.5 points as underdogs.

Florida International Panthers wide receiver Maguire Anderson (84) runs against the Penn State Nittany Lions | Matthew O'Haren-Imagn Images

FIU's defense has allowed 58 points through four games and held LIU to a lone field goal in a 20-3 win before the bye. "Another win, so I won't apologize for a win , but we once again did not play our best football, specifically on offense," FIU coach Willie Simmons said after the game. The Panthers still convert 47% of their third downs, while New Mexico State allows opponents to convert 42% of the time.

Quarterback JJ Kohl, a 6-foot-7 transfer from App State, suffered a grade-one MCL sprain against LIU but practiced during the off week. He also leads Conference USA with six interceptions, and FIU turned it over three times in each loss to USF and Florida Atlantic. New Mexico State (2-3, 1-0) enters off a 21-point home win over Western Kentucky, but the Aggies also committed three turnovers in losses to Hawaii and New Mexico.

Washington Huskies quarterback Demond Williams Jr. (1) passes the ball against the USC Trojans | Griffin Hooper-Imagn Images

Iowa ran for 39 yards on 21 carries in Saturday's 31-14 home loss to Ohio State, and quarterback Hank Brown completed 12 of 27 passes for 132 yards before leaving with a mild sprain. Brown remains atop the depth chart , but the No. 20 Hawkeyes now face a short-week trip roughly 2,000 miles from Iowa City.

Washington (3-2, 0-2) has lost two straight by a combined seven points, including a 25-21 loss at USC decided by a 48-yard fumble return touchdown. The Huskies' rushing attack ranks 124th nationally , so Demond Williams Jr. has to carry the offense against a defense that allowed 8 points per game through September. Still, Washington's defense gives up 16.8 points per game, and the spread has moved from Washington -1.5 to -3 since opening.

Utah State Aggies wide receiver Eli Wood (7) celebrates after catching a touchdown pass from quarterback Grady Brosterhous (9) during the fourth quarter at Husky Stadium. | Joe Nicholson-Imagn Images

Utah State and Washington State are both 1-4 and 0-1 in Pac-12 play, but their results against a common opponent favor the Aggies. Utah State lost 16-14 at Washington, while Washington State fell 24-10 to the Huskies in its opener. The Cougars also lost 26-6 at home to Fresno State last week, and quarterback Caden Pinnick has five interceptions against three touchdown passes.

Utah State coach Bronco Mendenhall's team has its own problems after an opening loss to FCS Idaho State and a 37-18 defeat at Boise State. "I haven't cracked that code," Mendenhall said of his team's mistakes in Boise. However, receiver Eli Wood has 388 yards and four touchdowns, and the Aggies host a Washington State offense that has scored 13 points across its last two games.

Iowa State Cyclones running back Aiden Flora (21) breaks through the West Virginia Mountaineers' defense for a touchdown during the second half at Jack Trice Stadium. | Reese Strickland-Imagn Images

No. 8 BYU is 4-0, but last week's 17-10 win at TCU was tied 7-7 at halftime, and running back LJ Martin left with an injury . Quarterback Bear Bachmeier has 704 passing yards and six touchdown passes, and he scored twice on the ground in Fort Worth.

First-year Iowa State coach Jimmy Rogers' Cyclones (3-2) lost 16-13 at Iowa and 31-17 to Utah, then rebounded with a home win over West Virginia. Iowa State also leads the all-time series 5-1 and is 3-0 in Provo, though BYU won 41-27 in Ames last season. The spread has dropped four points since opening and the total has fallen to 46.5, which points toward the low-scoring game Iowa State needs.

Nebraska Cornhuskers wide receiver Jacory Barney Jr. (2), quarterback Anthony Colandrea (10), wide receiver Kwazi Gilmer (3) and running back Mekhi Nelson (13) wait with teammates | Dylan Widger-Imagn Images

Nebraska (5-0, 2-0) is off to its best start since 2016 and has scored at least 30 points in every game. Quarterback Anthony Colandrea accounted for 346 yards and three touchdowns in a 48-23 win over Maryland, including a career-high 108 rushing yards. "We're going to make people defend our quarterback ," Nebraska coach Matt Rhule said Monday.

No. 7 Indiana carries the nation's longest active winning streak at 21 games, and quarterback Josh Hoover has 15 touchdown passes without an interception. However, Jeff Sagarin's ratings place the Hoosiers' schedule 103rd nationally and the Cornhuskers' 111th, so neither team has faced an opponent like this one. The spread has also dropped 2.5 points since opening, and Indiana's defense hasn't seen a quarterback run game like Colandrea's.

Alabama Crimson Tide wide receiver Ryan Coleman-Williams (1) celebrates with offensive lineman Jackson Lloyd (77) and quarterback Keelon Russell (12) after scoring a touchdown against the Mississippi State Bulldogs | Petre Thomas-Imagn Images

Alabama hasn't scored fewer than 45 points in a game this season, and Keelon Russell has thrown 10 touchdown passes in his last three starts. The sophomore quarterback is completing 71.2% of his passes for 1,414 yards, 11 touchdowns and two interceptions, which moved him into the top three of this SI Heisman Trophy tracker .

Georgia hasn't allowed more than 20 points in a game and has outscored opponents 70-7 in the first quarter. "This version has just jumped all over people ," Alabama coach Kalen DeBoer said of the Bulldogs.

But Georgia hasn't won in Tuscaloosa since 2007, and Alabama's defense leads the SEC with 13 takeaways. DeBoer's teams have won two of three meetings with Georgia coach Kirby Smart, including a 24-21 win last season before Georgia took the SEC Championship Game 28-7.

Game odds refresh periodically and are subject to change. If you or someone you know has a gambling problem and wants help, call 1-800-GAMBLER.

articles.title: Vanderbilt football announces sellout for homecoming game vs Arkansas
articles.summary: Vanderbilt football announced it has sold out its upcoming homecoming game vs. Arkansas.
articles.body:
Vanderbilt football announced Oct. 6 that it has sold out its ticket allotment for its upcoming homecoming game against Arkansas, set for Oct. 17.

There are no more tickets remaining from the school, with secondary tickets starting at $66 on StubHub .

That game will be held at 6 p.m. CT on ESPN2.

Inside Vanderbilt vs Georgia, with Jared Curtis out with injury in SEC game

The Commodores (3-2, 0-2 SEC) will first have their SEC home opener on Oct. 10 against Ole Miss . That game has not yet sold out, but less than 500 official tickets remain, according to the release.

Vanderbilt has wins in its three games at FirstBank Stadium this season against Austin Peay, Delaware and NC State. The Commodores have won 10 consecutive home games dating back to the start of 2025, which is the longest home win streak for the program since 1930.

Vanderbilt lost both of its road games so far this season to Auburn and Georgia.

Aria Gerson covers Vanderbilt athletics for The Tennessean. Contact her at agerson@gannett.com or on X @aria_gerson .
